prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Caldera Wildfire Detection and Suppression Support System (WUI, steep terrain). Baseline: segmentation, time sync, health checks, audit logs (assignment/staging changes reconstructable per crew); coordination records keep timestamps, participants, radio path; favor command continuity over automation when comms/power/sensors impaired. Elements: Caldera Incident Command Portal (Emberhall): common operating picture; produces Crew Staging Pin; triage; jurisdictional constraints; marks failed radio route impaired (Orion acknowledges); records assignment packages (objective, validity, confirmation, acknowledgments); Extended Attack preserves aviation decisions (supervisor, period, reason); flags assignments for review when Confirmed Ignition changes perimeter/priority; Disconnected Operating Mode if primary network lost: shows last sync time, cached review, queued updates, no irreversible releases. North Lookout Camera Mast: Thermal Spot Snippet. South Lookout Camera Mast: Camera Cleaning Log (to Smoke Classifier Module). Horizon Ridge Drone Dock (Kestrel): Battery Swap Ticket to Drone Pilot Operator; readiness/health/recovery before recon release; availability input only, never authorizes crew movement. Drone Tasking Service: builds missions; task status pending/active/complete; no flight-release authority; no conflict with Marigold lanes. Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine (Lantern): detection, recommendations, hazard summaries; Ridge Shadow Mask; may down-weight Smoke Classifier Module (never sole basis for aircraft commitment); crew exposure refresh only when recon confidence and weather timing valid; keeps last approved model on repository outage, rejects unversioned rules/unsigned packages. MesoWest Weather Fusion Node (Brindle): Wind Shift Bulletin to Redtail; exposure flags for ridgeline/drainage staging. VHF Radio Gateway Repeater (Badger): fallback aviation relay; mirrors priority assignment summaries to crews without data. Talon Air Tanker Dispatch Console (Marigold): blocks plan release if approvals/airspace/tanker readiness incomplete; Runway Release Note; Suppression Drop Receipt after drop recorded, timing checked. East (Retardant Batch Slip)/West Retardant Loading Pumps: informational. Crewline Mobile Tablet: acknowledgements; objectives, hazards (snags, access, slope, utilities, escape routes), division, route, rally point, channel; caches staging; expired packages unavailable; degraded link shows last verified package with update time. Actors: County Emergency Liaison (Drone Corridor Permit; view-only staging/public safety). Duty Detection Officer (Orion): warned of

New part:
S181: The Smoke Classifier Module shall label detections as advisory when either camera mast is unavailable or when image quality falls below the validated threshold.
S182: The North Lookout Camera Mast and the South Lookout Camera Mast shall report heartbeat, temperature, storage, and pointing-status telemetry so that maintenance staff can distinguish sensor failure from environmental obscuration.
S183: The MesoWest Weather Fusion Node shall retain a local weather cache sufficient to support near-term fire behavior review when upstream feeds are intermittent.
S184: Crewline Mobile Tablet clients shall queue field updates locally, encrypt the queue at rest, and reconcile conflicts by preserving the original author, device time, and server acceptance time.
S185: All interactive access to the Caldera Incident Command Portal requires named accounts, role-based authorization, and multifactor authentication when the authentication service is reachable.
S186: When the authentication service is unreachable, emergency access uses pre-issued signed credentials that expire automatically and require supervisor review after restoration.
S187: The Air Attack Supervisor, Tanker Base Manager, Helitack Crew Leader, Drone Pilot Operator, and County Emergency Liaison receive only the permissions required for their operational responsibilities.
S188: Administrative privileges for production configuration changes require separate approval from operational command roles and are not granted through field user accounts.
S189: Security-relevant events, including failed logons, role changes, queued update releases, model changes, and maintenance overrides, shall be written to an append-only audit store.
S190: Audit records shall include synchronized time, user identity, device identity, source network, affected record, and outcome so that incident reconstruction remains possible after the event.
S191: If central audit storage is unavailable, each field component shall buffer signed audit records locally and forward them without modification when connectivity returns.
S192: Drone Tasking Service validates the corridor permit before releasing an automated flight task in degraded communications mode.
S193: Badger shall queue outbound voice-to-data acknowledgments for at least fifteen minutes during backhaul loss and forward them when the link is restored.
S194: East Retardant Loading Pump shall enter a metered recirculation mode when pressure variance exceeds the calibrated maintenance limit.
S195: The West Retardant Loading Pump shall be inspected at shift change for hose wear, valve position, controller alarms, and leakage before it is returned to operational availability.
S196: Maintenance actions on field equipment shall be recorded with technician identity, time, observed condition, corrective action, and verification result before the equipment status is changed.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
